introduction.text: In this lesson, you will learn about the passive voice in German, specifically using the verb 'werden.' You will understand how to form sentences in the passive voice and when to use them in everyday conversation related to work and career.
introduction.culturalNote: In Germany, the passive voice is often used in job descriptions and formal communication, making it an important aspect of professional language.

vocabulary.tip: Remember that 'der Vertrag' is masculine, so use 'der' for the article.

vocabulary.tip: 'Die Bewerbung' is feminine, so remember to use 'die' for the article.

vocabulary.tip: This word is masculine; use 'der' for the article.

vocabulary.tip: 'Die Stelle' is feminine; use 'die' for the article.

vocabulary.tip: This word is feminine, so remember to use 'die' for the article.

vocabulary.definition: Information about reactions to a product or service.
vocabulary.tip: 'Das Feedback' is neuter; use 'das' for the article.

grammar.title: The Passive Voice (Werden)
grammar.explanation: In German, the passive voice is used to emphasize the action rather than the subject performing the action. The passive is formed with the verb 'werden' followed by the past participle of the main verb. For example, 'Der Brief wird geschrieben' means 'The letter is being written.' The focus is on the letter, not who is writing it.

rows: Der Bericht wird (von dem Chef) geschrieben.

examples.breakdown: Here, 'wird' (is) + 'durchgeführt' (conducted) shows that the training is the focus.
In this case, 'wird' (is) + 'unterschrieben' (signed) indicates the action performed on the contract.

commonMistakes: Using the wrong form of 'werden': Ensure you use the correct tense of 'werden' based on the subject and time.
Confusing active and passive: Remember that in passive sentences, the subject receives the action rather than performing it.

dialogue.title: Discussing Job Applications
dialogue.context: Two colleagues, Anna and Max, are talking about their job applications during lunch.

lines.text: Hast du deine Bewerbung schon abgeschickt?
lines.translation: Have you already sent your application?

lines.text: Ja, sie wurde letzte Woche abgeschickt.
lines.translation: Yes, it was sent last week.

lines.text: Nein, das Feedback wird noch erwartet.
lines.translation: No, the feedback is still expected.

lines.text: Ich habe gehört, dass die Stelle bald besetzt wird.
lines.translation: I heard that the position will be filled soon.

lines.text: Das wäre gut! Ich hoffe, dass ich ausgewählt werde.
lines.translation: That would be good! I hope that I will be chosen.

lines.text: Wenn du ein Interview bekommst, wird dir alles erklärt.
lines.translation: If you get an interview, everything will be explained to you.

lines.text: Ja, das habe ich auch gehört. Ich bin gespannt!
lines.translation: Yes, I have heard that too. I am excited!

culture.title: The Importance of the Passive Voice in Professional Settings
culture.text: In German-speaking countries, formal communication often employs the passive voice, especially in business contexts. Job descriptions and official documents frequently use this construction to maintain a neutral tone.
culture.funFact: In Germany, many companies emphasize teamwork and collaboration, which is often reflected in the use of passive constructions to highlight group efforts.

keyPoints: The passive voice emphasizes the action rather than the subject.
Use 'werden' with the past participle to form passive sentences.
The passive is common in job-related contexts.
Remember to pay attention to the gender and articles of nouns.
summary.nextSteps: Practice forming passive sentences using the vocabulary from this lesson. Try to create sentences about your own work or career experiences.
